S1.lab_notes: z_T uses log_ret[T] (known at close T), mu and sigma computed over [T-Nz, T-1] (shift(1)); vol-gate similarly uses past data. Entry at next open (T+1). No leak.

S2.lab_notes: r_T and V_T known at close T; vol_avg over [T-Nv, T-1] (shift(1)). Entry at next open. No leak.

S3.lab_notes: g_T = O_T/C_{T-1}-1 known at open T (needed for signal); C_T, H_T, L_T known at close T. Signal computed after close T. Entry at C_T (or next open). MARGINAL CONCERN: entry at C_T on bar T uses bar-T close which requires waiting for the close — acceptable for end-of-day execution; entry at NEXT OPEN is clean and preferred. No fundamental look-ahead.

S4.lab_notes: LOOK-AHEAD FLAG: VR computation uses a rolling 5-bar sum via pd.Series.rolling(5).sum() applied to shift(1) series. The VR numerator Var(5-day ret) computed over 60 bars uses OVERLAPPING 5-day windows. With overlapping windows, the variance estimator at bar T includes information from bars T+1..T+4 in some sub-windows when computed naively. In the hypothesis text, VR is defined as Var(sum_{i=0}^{q-1} r_{t-i}) — this includes r_t itself in the sum, making the 5-day return end at bar t. When rolled as Var over 60 bars ending at T (with the shift(1) applied to r only), the last VR data point uses r_T in one of its 5-bar windows. This is a subtle but real look-ahead: the most recent 5-bar block (including r_T) feeds VR_T. r_T IS known at close T, so TECHNICALLY it is not future data, but using r_T (bar T's own return) in the VR used to decide entry at T means you are conditioning the regime call on the very return that would contribute to regime classification ONLY if you already traded. This is a contemporaneous-bar contamination. Industry standard is to require VR computed as of T-1 (rolling window ends at T-1). The hypothesis text says 'estimated over the trailing N_VR bars' which is ambiguous but most conservative interpretation is end at T, giving a contemporaneous leak. VERDICT: FAIL — contemporaneous VR contaminates signal at bar T; regime call is data-snooped on the same bar's return.

S5.lab_notes: Channel HH/LL from [T-N_ch, T-1] (shift(1)); compression ratio uses bars [T-Nc+1, T-1] and [T-Nb, T-Nc+1] (all past). C_T and V_T known at close T; breakout check is C_T > HH_T (prior channel). Entry at C_T or next open. No look-ahead.

S6.lab_notes: 52-week high from C_{T-1} backward (shift(1)); pi_ratio = C_T / max_past. C_T known at close T. Entry at next open. No look-ahead. HOWEVER: uses raw close C_T (not adjusted_close) for the 252-day high. Since no corporate actions are in splits/dividends tables, adjusted_close IS close (no adjustments applied), so this is consistent.

S7.lab_notes: Leader composite uses bar-T closes (known at T); laggard trades next open. Cross-sectional computation uses only same-day or prior-day data. Correlation matrix estimated over prior N_corr bars. No look-ahead.

S8.lab_notes: Beta estimated over [T-N_beta, T-1] (strictly past); residual at T uses r_T and mkt_ret_T (both known at close T). z_resid uses rolling mean/std of residuals over [T-N_rz, T-1] (shift(1)). Entry at next open. No leak.

S9.lab_notes: RV percentile from strictly-past (shift(1)) series; BB bands from shift(1) SMA/std of adjusted_close. A_T (current close) compared to past bands — current price known at T. Not-breakout filter reuses prior-channel. No look-ahead.

S10.lab_notes: Hurst estimated on rolling trailing window (past returns). In our implementation, Hurst is approximated via the same VR estimator as S4, BUT we apply it correctly with shift(1) so VR at bar T uses returns through T-1 only. Direction = A_T/A_{T-20} - 1, which uses A_T (current close) compared to 20 bars ago — both known at T. Entry at next open. Clean. NOTE: The VR proxy for Hurst is an approximation; true R/S or DFA should be used in production but does not change the bias assessment.

S11.lab_notes: Turnover U_T = C_T * V_T known at close T; avg over [T-N_tau, T-1] (shift(1)). pp3 = sum of log_ret[T-2..T] includes r_T which is known at close T. Entry at next open. No fundamental look-ahead.
